reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Counting renal and liver as one point.
Using the score to withhold anticoagulation without weighing stroke risk.
name: HAS-BLED Bleeding Risk Score

version.label: HAS-BLED (Pisters et al. 2010)
version.detail: Nine items, one point each, total 0–9. Abnormal renal and liver function, and drugs and alcohol, are scored separately.

purpose: Estimates 1-year major bleeding risk in patients with atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation.
intendedPopulation: Adults with atrial fibrillation considered for or taking anticoagulation.

inputDefinitions.label: Abnormal renal function (dialysis, transplant or creatinine ≥200 µmol/L)
Abnormal liver function (cirrhosis, or bilirubin >2× and AST/ALT/ALP >3× normal)
Drugs predisposing to bleeding (antiplatelet agents, NSAIDs)

resultStates.label: HAS-BLED {total}
resultStates.detail: Bleeding risk still depends on factors not in the score.

resultStates.label: High bleeding risk (≥3)
resultStates.summary: HAS-BLED 3 or more: high-risk group in the derivation study.
resultStates.detail: In guidelines this flags the need to correct modifiable factors and review more often; on its own it is not a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Integrate with stroke risk.

clinicalContext.text: Identifies patients with higher bleeding risk on anticoagulation, and modifiable factors.

clinicalInsights.text: Some contributing factors are modifiable (blood pressure, INR control, concomitant drugs, alcohol).

limitations.text: Moderate predictive accuracy; not a decision rule for withholding anticoagulation.

limitations: Labile INR applies only to vitamin K antagonists.

guideSections.what: Nine bleeding risk factors, one point each.
guideSections.whenToUse: Atrial fibrillation patients on or considered for anticoagulation.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with CHA₂DS₂-VASc and to target modifiable risk.

sources.citation: Pisters R, Lane DA, Nieuwlaat R, de Vos CB, Crijns HJGM, Lip GYH. A novel user-friendly score (HAS-BLED) to assess 1-year risk of major bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation: the Euro Heart Survey. Chest. 2010;138(5):1093-1100.
